How much does a basement renovation cost in Ontario?

Most of the price comes down to a handful of things: size, adding a bathroom, building a legal second unit, waterproofing, egress windows and relocating plumbing. Two basements the same size can be far apart in price, so we don't quote by the square foot over the phone. We give you a fixed written price after a free site visit.
Do I need a building permit for my renovation?

Often, yes. Under the Ontario Building Code you need a permit to finish a basement with a new bathroom or second unit, to remove or alter a structural wall, for most new plumbing, and for a deck attached to the house or more than 60 cm above grade. Flooring, cabinets and paint usually do not. When a permit is needed, we apply for it, book the inspections and show the fee on the quote.
How long does a kitchen renovation take?
It depends on how much of the room moves, since keeping the layout is quicker than moving walls or plumbing. Your quote gives you a start date and a finish date in writing.
Is LVP or hardwood better for a basement?

LVP, in most basements. It is waterproof, it floats over the slab and it shrugs off the humidity swings that come with being below grade. Solid hardwood should not go on a concrete slab. Engineered hardwood can work over a dry slab with a proper subfloor if you want real wood underfoot, but it costs more and is less forgiving if water ever gets in.
Should I get a concrete patio or interlock?

Poured concrete costs less up front and lasts for decades if it is air-entrained and placed on a properly compacted base. Interlock costs more, but single pavers can be lifted and relaid if the ground settles, and it does not crack the way a slab can. For a plain rectangle, concrete is good value. For curves, steps or soft ground, interlock is usually the better call.
Do you handle design, or do I need a designer?

We handle layout and finish selections for most kitchens, bathrooms and basements, and you see drawings before you sign anything. For additions or structural changes we bring in an engineer or architect and coordinate their drawings with the permit. If you already have a designer, we build from their plans.
